formation.explanation: Leader dispatch assigns term/index, persists logs and records local match. Replication success records peer match in the term-specific commitment object. The configured voter order statistic advances commitment only after reaching the current-term startIndex. Main-loop notification enqueues committed inflight entries to the FSM and propagates commit index in later AppendEntries. Followers validate predecessor history, replace conflicts and apply through the bounded leader commit index. Future completion and application occur asynchronously after enqueue.

context.explanation: Follower timeout can start a voter election. Pre-vote normally precedes persisted term advancement and actual votes. Each election has its own reply channel; requestVote checks candidate membership, term, durable vote and log freshness. Quorum grants acquire leader role. Incoming higher-term requests and replication replies can cause loss of authority. Leader entry creates fresh accounting; exit stops replicators and fails outstanding operations. Leadership transfer and concurrent heartbeat dispatch require further tracing.

connection.explanation: Only voters in the current configuration contribute to formation. Reconfiguration is serialized behind committed membership and a current-term entry, then changes quorum eligibility while retaining surviving IDs support. Old replication completions target their captured old commitment object rather than a new leader object. Persistent logs and snapshot metadata constrain future freshness and reconstruction; losing a future does not erase a potentially surviving log entry. Snapshot restoration resets application/history context only after FSM restore completion.

Incoming vote and append requests qualify term and history; higher-term replication replies signal stepdown. Leader entry owns fresh accounting and exit stops replication and fails pending operations. Lease checks voter contact. Transfer catches the selected voter up using its replication object then sends TimeoutNow; receiver marks a transfer campaign that bypasses pre-vote, and campaign exit clears that flag. A separate monitor requests worker stop on timeout/leader-loop exit and waits for completion, but cannot cancel TimeoutNow itself. Network transport concurrently delivers only empty zero-commit heartbeats; atomics/locks protect individual state fields, while compound term-update ordering remains an open local premise.

User restore is an explicit history replacement that aborts inflight requests and burns an index to force follower resynchronization; routine snapshots instead persist applied state and committed configuration before compaction.

Incoming vote and append requests qualify term and history; higher-term replication replies signal stepdown. Leader entry owns fresh accounting and exit stops replication and fails pending operations. Lease checks voter contact. Transfer catches the selected voter up using its replication object then sends TimeoutNow; receiver marks a transfer campaign that bypasses pre-vote, and campaign exit clears that flag. A separate monitor requests worker stop on timeout/leader-loop exit and waits for completion, but cannot cancel TimeoutNow itself. User restore is an explicit history replacement that aborts inflight requests and burns an index to force follower resynchronization; routine snapshots instead persist applied state and committed configuration before compaction.
